newsitem.title: USA: Senators ask Clinton to prevent AMR strike.
newsitem.headline: Senators ask Clinton to prevent AMR strike.

text.p: Florida Senators Bob Graham and Connie Mack on Friday asked President Clinton to help AMR Corp's American Airlines and its pilots reach a settlement to avoid a strike that would cripple Florida's winter tourism business.

American is based outside Fort Worth, Texas, but is the dominant air carrier at Miami International Airport, a key gateway for passengers and cargo to Latin America. In a letter to the president, Graham and Mack said a strike beginning February 15 would be "costly" and "painful."

"If a settlement is not reached, a mid-February holiday weekend airline strike would disrupt passengers and the flow of freight across our nation and overseas, particularly in our hemisphere," the letter said. "Nowhere would the harm be more acute than in Florida."

Pilots' leaders have said they want to win a new contract now, even if it involves a strike, rather than risk lengthy arbitration. Earlier this week, a senior union leader forecast a 50 percent possibility of a strike and that it could last up to 60 days.

Starting Monday, the two sides are to begin five days of "supermediation" in a last-gasp effort to reach a new four-year labor contract. Those negotiations will take place in Washington with the help of the National Mediation Board.

Pilots are demanding pay raises of more than 11 percent over the life of the contract, improved stock options and a guarantee that American will not use its American Eagle commuter carrier, which employs pilots of another union, to fly 50-passenger regional jets.
